title: Breaking Apart Numbers
short: Split a number like 5 into 2 and 3, or 4 and 1.
trouble: Children find only one way to split a number and think it is the only answer.

blocks.html: When you put together two parts, you make a whole. You can also break a whole apart into two parts.

blocks.name: numberbond
blocks.cap: The top circle is the whole. The bottom circles are the parts. Drag the line in the beads to split 5 a new way.

blocks.html: A number can be broken into two parts in more than one way. 5 is 4 and 1, or 3 and 2, or 2 and 3, or 1 and 4, or 5 and 0.
Moving one bead from one part to the other does not change the whole. So many different pairs make the same number.

blocks.title: All the ways to make 4
blocks.q: Find all the ways to break 4 into two parts.

blocks.html: Finding one way and stopping, as if it were the only answer. There are many! Move one counter from one part to the other and say the new pair.
For grown-ups: Hide some of 5 pennies under a cup. Your child says how many are hiding. Then try all the other ways.

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Kindergarten, K.OA.A.3: decompose numbers up to 10 into pairs in more than one way
